  PROBLEM: The floor clamp unconditionally raises `reviewer_embed_budget_bytes` to `REVIEWER_PROMPT_EMBED_BUDGET_FLOOR_BYTES`, even when the computed budget is below zero or below the cap-safe value.
  WHY: That can make the assembled prompt exceed the codex stdin cap and reintroduce the exact oversize failure this PR is meant to prevent; reviewers split across BLOCKER/CRITICAL/MAJOR, so the highest severity is critical.

- File: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh
Line or code reference: 1895-1897
Problem: Three new integer-threshold environment variables (`REVIEWER_PROMPT_CODEX_STDIN_CAP_BYTES`, `REVIEWER_PROMPT_SCAFFOLD_RESERVE_BYTES`, `REVIEWER_PROMPT_EMBED_BUDGET_FLOOR_BYTES`) are read via bare `${VAR:-default}` expansion and then used directly in bash arithmetic expansion and integer comparisons without validation.
Why it fails at runtime: Under `set -euo pipefail`, a non-numeric override such as `REVIEWER_PROMPT_CODEX_STDIN_CAP_BYTES=1_048_576` will trigger a bash arithmetic syntax error and abort the entire reviewer step before any model runs.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER

Why it fails at runtime: If the static prefix grows large enough, forcing the floor can make the assembled prompt exceed the codex stdin cap and reintroduce the oversize failure this PR is meant to prevent.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
